name: RideCard
purpose: Move's ride option, and one radio in a group. A rider chooses exactly one of several ways to make the same journey, so the card is the label of a real radio input rather than a box with a click handler — which is what v0 shipped and what made the ride selector unusable without a pointer.
responsibilities: Render a real <input type="radio"> whose label is the whole card, so the platform supplies the tab stop, the arrow keys, aria-checked and the disabled semantics.
Show one journey option: the vehicle, the tier, how far away it is, what it will cost and how many it seats.
Say when a fare is raised by demand, and attach that to the option rather than beside it.
Nothing about formatting. Every number arrives already formatted through the boundary content/rules/rtl-arabic.md §4 sets out.
Nothing about which option is chosen. That is the group's state and the caller's.
do: Put every option for one journey in a single RideCardGroup, so they share a name and behave as one choice.
Give the group a label. It becomes a real <legend>, and it is the only thing that says what is being chosen.
Pass eta, fare and capacity already formatted — Arabic has six plural categories, and a component cannot select between them.
Use disabled for a tier with no vehicle nearby, so the platform skips it during arrow-key navigation.
Pass surgeNote whenever a fare is raised, so the reason travels with the option through aria-describedby.
dont: Do not put a button, a link or any other control inside this card. It is a radio, and interactive content nested in a radio has no behaviour a user can reach — that is decision 024's argument and it is structural rather than stylistic.
Do not use it to display a ride nobody is choosing. A completed trip or a scheduled booking is a different component; this one is a control.

Do not pass a number to eta or capacity and let this component write the words. v0 does, with a hand-written special case for one seat, which is a two-category plural rule in a product that ships a six-category language.
Do not map a ride-type key to a label in here. v0 holds RIDE_TYPE_LABELS and falls back to the raw key, so an unrecognised tier renders as 'economy' in the middle of a translated interface.
Do not reach for mobility.* colours to carry a sentence. mobility.surge is declared at the 3.0 indicator bar and sits at 3.87:1 in dark, so it marks the note and text.secondary sets it.

do_not_use_when.when: The card must contain a button, a link, or any second interactive target.
do_not_use_when.use_instead: ProductCard, or a plain container. A radio may not contain a control — decision 024.

do_not_use_when.when: A ride is being displayed rather than chosen — a receipt, a trip in progress, a scheduled booking.
do_not_use_when.use_instead: Nothing yet. That component does not exist, and decision 024 records that it might be closer to ProductCard than to this.

do_not_use_when.when: The user may pick more than one option.
do_not_use_when.use_instead: A checkbox-based control. A radio group is exclusive by definition, and making this multi-select changes what element it is.
Plain content. A choice of one is not a choice, and a radio that cannot be unchecked is a control with nothing to do.
ProductCard. This component names mobility.* tokens, which only Move has.

alternatives.for: a Market product tile, which is a container holding a link and an action
a choice where more than one option may be picked
a ride being shown rather than chosen

content: The vehicle, as a rider will recognise it at the curb.
The tier name, which is a string from the catalogue rather than a key mapped in here.
The ETA, the fare and the capacity, each already formatted.
The surge note, which says why a fare is higher than usual.
constraints: No width and no fixed height. §6: a control sized to Latin ink clips Arabic, and the vertical axis clips rather than reflows.
No className and no style. The props type does not extend InputHTMLAttributes, which would hand back size — a width in characters.
No numbers. eta, fare and capacity are nodes, already formatted by §4's one boundary.
No nested interactive content, ever. It is a radio.
No colour that content/tokens/pairs.json has not seen, and none used outside the context it was declared in.
No click handler on the card. The label forwards activation to the input, which is what makes the keyboard work.
One written number, the 1px control edge, because there is still no border-width scale.

behaviour: Logical properties throughout. The rows are flex with space-between, which names an axis rather than a side, and the surge mark is a border-inline-start so it sits on the reading-start edge in both directions.
The fare carries unicode-bidi: isolate — the CSS equivalent of the <bdi> §3 asks for — because a formatted amount is the one run in this card guaranteed to be opposite-direction in Arabic.
The vehicle name is a ReactNode so a caller can wrap a Latin name in <bdi> when it sits inside a longer Arabic run.
letter-spacing 0, always, declared so it cannot be inherited from a page.
There is no [dir='rtl'] selector anywhere in the component.
mirrors: The whole card, with the document.
The surge mark, which follows the reading-start edge.
does_not_mirror: Nothing. There is no glyph in this component whose form carries meaning.

guarantees: A real <input type="radio"> inside a <label>, so one tab stop serves the group, arrow keys move between options, and aria-checked is the platform's.
The radio is visually hidden with a clip-rect rather than display:none, so it stays focusable and announced — display:none would reintroduce exactly the defect this component replaces.
A real <fieldset> and <legend> through RideCardGroup, which is what gives a set of radios one accessible name.
The surge note is linked with aria-describedby, so a rider is told an option is surging while they are on it rather than after.
Disabled uses the real attribute, so arrow-key navigation skips an option nobody can book.
The focus indicator is drawn on the card from the state of the hidden input, so the visible ring matches the thing that actually has focus.
0 axe violations across all six stories, checked in dark + Move + RTL.
consumer_must: Give the group a label. It is required by the type, but a label that does not say what is being chosen satisfies the type and not the user.
Pass every number already formatted. This component cannot select an Arabic plural category and will render whatever string it is handed.
Keep every option for one journey inside one group. Two groups on a screen are two independent choices, which is a different question from the one the screen is asking.

props.name: capacity
notes: A node for the same reason `eta` is: v0 writes `seats + ' seats'` with a hand-written special case for `1 seat`, which is a two-category plural rule in a product that ships a six-category language.
props.guidance: Already formatted, for the same plural reason as eta. v0 special-cases '1 seat' by hand.

props.name: checked
props.description: Whether this option is the chosen one.
props.guidance: Whether this is the chosen option. The card styles itself from the input's :checked state through :has(), so the DOM is the single source of truth and nothing in React mirrors it into a class that could disagree.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The option is not available — no vehicle of this tier nearby.
props.guidance: No vehicle of this tier nearby. The real attribute, so arrow-key navigation skips it — a rider does not land on a ride they cannot book.

props.name: eta
props.description: How far away the vehicle is, already formatted.
notes: **Not a number.** v0 writes `etaMinutes + ' min away'`, which is English concatenation with nowhere to put a plural category — and Arabic has six, including a dual, so "2 minutes" is not "3 minutes" with the number swapped. `content/rules/rtl-arabic.md` §4 puts every number behind one formatting boundary and records duration formatting as blocked on a string catalogue. This prop takes what that boundary produced.
props.guidance: Already formatted. v0 writes etaMinutes + ' min away', which is English concatenation with nowhere to put a plural category, and Arabic has six including a dual.

props.name: fare
props.description: The fare, already formatted by the §4 boundary — `AED 24.00`, or `24.00 د.إ` in Arabic, with the symbol placed by `Intl` rather than concatenated.
props.guidance: Already formatted by §4's boundary — symbol placed by Intl, Western digits in both locales, the currency's own minor-unit count. Isolated in CSS because it is the one run here guaranteed to be opposite-direction in Arabic.

props.name: fareBasis
props.description: Whether the fare is an estimate or settled. Defaults to `'estimate'`, because that is what every fare Move currently shows actually is.
props.guidance: Estimate or settled. Every fare Move currently shows is an estimate, and saying so is a decision rather than a default: a rider who reads a provisional fare as fixed has been misled by the interface.

props.name: name
props.description: The group name. **Every card in one choice shares it**, and that shared name is what makes the browser treat them as one radio group: a single tab stop for the whole set, arrow keys moving between options, and exactly one chosen. None of that is implemented here — it is the platform's, and it is the reason this component is a real `<input type="radio">` rather than a `div` with `role="radio"` and a key handler that would have to reimplement all of it.
notes: `RideCardGroup` sets this for its children, so a call site normally does not.
props.guidance: Shared by every card in one choice, which is what makes the browser treat them as one radio group. RideCardGroup sets it, so a call site normally does not — a call site repeating it by hand is one where the fifth card gets a typo and silently becomes its own group of one.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Chosen. Reports the `value` of whichever card the user picked.
props.guidance: Reports the value of whichever card the user picked.

props.name: rideType
props.description: The tier — Economy, Comfort, XL, Electric.
notes: Taken as a node rather than mapped from a key inside this component. v0 holds a `RIDE_TYPE_LABELS` object and falls back to the raw key when a type is missing from it, which means an unrecognised tier renders as `economy` in the middle of a translated interface. A label is a string from the catalogue and the catalogue is not this component's business.
props.guidance: The tier. A string from the catalogue rather than a key this component maps — v0 maps it and falls back to the raw key, so an unrecognised tier renders as 'economy' mid-translation.

props.name: surgeNote
props.description: Why the fare is higher than usual, when it is — Move's surge note.
notes: Painted in `mobility.surge`, which this component is allowed to reference and a shared one is not. That permission is a consequence of decision 024 rather than an incidental convenience: keeping this component Move's is what lets it name Move's tokens.
props.guidance: Why the fare is higher. Marked with mobility.surge and set in text.secondary — the token is declared at the 3.0 indicator bar and cannot carry a sentence, which axe caught after the first version painted the whole note with it.

props.name: value
props.description: The value this option submits, and what `onChange` reports. Unique within the group.
props.guidance: What this option submits. Unique within the group and never shown.

props.name: vehicle
props.description: The vehicle, as the rider will recognise it at the curb — "Toyota Camry".
notes: A `ReactNode` rather than a string so it can carry a `<bdi>`-wrapped run. A vehicle name is Latin in an Arabic interface more often than not, and §3 is explicit that a run of opposite-direction content inside a sentence is isolated rather than hoped about.
props.guidance: What the rider will recognise at the curb. A node, so a Latin name inside an Arabic run can be wrapped in <bdi> by the caller.

unmapped.why: A form value has no visual form.
The group name is plumbing that makes four radios one choice. Nothing about it is drawn.
A handler is behaviour. Figma properties describe what a component looks like.

use_when: A rider chooses one of several ways to make the same journey.
A Move booking screen needs its ride selector.
A set of options is exclusive and each needs more than a line of text.
not_a: A product tile. That is ProductCard and it is a container, not a control.
A container for other controls. A card whose whole surface selects it cannot also contain an independently operable button.
A display of a ride nobody is choosing.

deprecation.policy: It replaces v0's RideCard and is withdrawn only by a decision naming what replaces it. A prop is withdrawn ahead of the component: mark it @deprecated in the source with the replacement named in the tag, keep it working for one minor version, then remove it in a major one with the migration written down. The prop most likely to move is fareBasis, which currently has two values and would gain a third rather than a sibling prop.
